parent_domains.justification: Neurodevelopment is fundamentally a part of neuroscience as it deals with the development of the nervous system.
The plural form ‘neurosciences’ is a broad category under which neurodevelopment naturally falls.
Neurodevelopment can be studied and modeled using computational neuroscience techniques, as development involves complex neural computations.

closest_parent_domain.justification: As neurodevelopment is essentially about the development of the nervous system, it is most closely associated with the broader domain of neuroscience.

child_domains.justification: Neurodevelopmental disorders arise from issues in the neurodevelopmental processes, making them a direct subcategory.

closest_child_domain.justification: This domain directly describes conditions arising from problems in the process of neurodevelopment, making it the closest child domain.

sibling_domains.justification: Neuroanatomy is closely related to neurodevelopment as both deal with the structure of the nervous system.
This area is related as both domains often collaborate to visualize and track neurodevelopment processes.
Synaptic plasticity is a critical aspect of neurodevelopment, especially in the formation and reformation of synapses.
Neurodevelopment plays a crucial role in forming brain structure, making this a sibling domain.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Neuroanatomy closely complements neurodevelopment, as understanding the anatomy is essential to studying how the nervous system develops.

unrelated_domains.justification: While related to brain function, these disorders do not directly pertain to neurodevelopment processes.
Neurology is more concerned with diseases of the nervous system rather than its development.
Neuroergonomics focuses on applying neuroscience principles rather than studying the development of the nervous system.
Neuro-AI focuses on artificial intelligence inspired by neuroscience, not directly on neurodevelopment.
